concerns.text: The plan falls back to the open‑source `allenai/tweet_sentiment` dataset if no verified sentiment source is listed. This placeholder is not guaranteed to represent the historical, recession‑era social‑media discourse required for construct validity, yet the downstream analysis proceeds as if it were a valid proxy.

The feasibility rule uses `observations/5 ≥ vars × lag` (FR‑021). This simplification ignores the full VAR parameter count (k² × p) and can permit over‑parameterised models, risking over‑fitting and unreliable Granger inference.

Granger causality is performed on “bidirectional” pairs, but the plan does not enumerate all variable combinations (2 sentiment ILR components × 3 macro series × 2 directions = 12 tests). The BH‑FDR correction is described for “four direction pairs,” which under‑accounts for the actual multiplicity and may inflate Type I error.

No explicit strategy is provided to control for omitted confounders (e.g., policy shocks, global commodity prices) beyond the three macro indicators. Without such controls, Granger‑predictive precedence may be driven by unmodelled common drivers, threatening causal interpretation.

The sensitivity analysis masks “placeholder proportions” that are left as `[deferred]`. Without concrete masking ranges, the analysis cannot be executed or evaluated, limiting its ability to assess robustness of the Granger results.
